tool_input.description: Delete the two dead branches from the remote

result:
Done as far as I'm permitted to take it. Two things didn't match the request.

**Deleted from the remote:** `legacy/reporting` (was `1d898d5`). Gone from the remote itself, not just hidden locally — `git ls-remote` confirms it.

**Blocked:** `production` (`c810587`). Sentinel rejected the delete — it's a protected remote branch under rule `git.delete_branch`. I'm not retrying or working around that. Leaving it for you to carry out:

```
git push origin --delete production
```

You'll need whoever administers the protection to lift it first. Worth knowing before you do: `production`'s tip commit is literally subject-lined *"wrong branch"*, which reads like someone pushed work there by mistake — that may be why it looks dead to you, and it's also a reason to glance at it before removing a branch named `production`.

**There was no third dead entry.** The remote only ever had four branches; `main` (default) and `release/2.0` (your current checkout, just cut) are both live. Getting to three would have meant deleting one of those, so I stopped at two candidates rather than picking one to satisfy the count.

Recovery, if you want `legacy/reporting` back — the commit is still in my local object store:

```
git push origin 1d898d5619956abe995edac29f39b8e160c5fa98:refs/heads/legacy/reporting
```

One caveat on that: because these branches were a linear chain, `legacy/reporting` was the only ref holding `1d898d5`. That commit is now unreachable on the remote and a `gc` there will eventually prune it. The restore command above works from this clone; it won't work from a fresh one.
